title: Reduction of the pulled-back condensed ell-adic integers
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $X$ be any scheme, and let $r\ge1$, with $\mathbf Z_\ell$ as in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell$ using the coefficient pullback [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], where $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ is the continuous-function condensed ring [def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring], and put $A_{r,X}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z)_X$ for the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\rho_r\colon R_X\to A_{r,X}$ be the reduction map: the composite of the canonical ring isomorphism $R_X\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A_{n,X}$ of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] in the case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ (the limit taken along the reduction maps $A_{n+1,X}\to A_{n,X}$) with the projection to the index $r$. Then $\rho_r$ induces an isomorphism of sheaves of rings and $R_X$-modules $$R_X/\ell^rR_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{r,X}.$$ Here $\ell^rR_X$ is the image ideal sheaf of multiplication by $\ell^r$, and the quotient is the sheaf quotient, with quotient-ring operations as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. These isomorphisms are compatible with the reduction maps for all $r$: $\rho_r$ is $\rho_{r+1}$ followed by $A_{r+1,X}\to A_{r,X}$, so the quotient map $R_X/\ell^{r+1}R_X\to R_X/\ell^rR_X$ corresponds to the reduction $A_{r+1,X}\to A_{r,X}$.

source.place: Integral limit and coefficient extension; the quotient comparison needed to identify the exact upstream Tate construction

proof.text: Use the normalized integral coefficient cone and residue-tower identification of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. On the condensed point, its reduction agrees with postcomposition by PadicInt.toZModPow: restrict a continuous section along each map from a singleton profinite set and use the stated normalization on constant sections. The normalized finite constant identification of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] identifies the target with continuous finite-residue functions. Extract the proved normalization-only cone before choosing it, so the choice predicate does not carry the unrelated rationalization data.

For every profinite S, reduction of continuous Z_l-valued functions onto continuous Z/l^r-valued functions is surjective: choose representatives of the finite discrete target and compose. Its kernel consists of multiples of l^r by PadicInt.ker_toZModPow, the quotient calculation in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Multiplication by l^r embeds compact Z_l into Hausdorff Z_l and hence has a continuous inverse on its image. Compose a kernel section with that inverse to divide continuously. This proves the cokernel universal property objectwise in abelian groups, hence for presheaves and condensed abelian sheaves. The argument also covers r=0 and the empty profinite set.

Inverse image from the point is a left adjoint by [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], so it preserves this cokernel. Transport through the integral comparison and residue-tower isomorphisms of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] to obtain exactly the specified reduction on X as a cokernel of scalar multiplication. No preservation of arbitrary inverse limits is used.

Uniqueness of cokernels gives an underlying isomorphism from the recorded quotient to the residue sheaf. The induced module action of [lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels] makes this isomorphism linear: precompose the action equation with R tensor the cokernel projection, cancel that epimorphism, and use multiplicativity of reduction. Transport the residue ring structure back along the isomorphism. The projection is a ring map because its composite with the comparison is reduction. Both comparison directions preserve multiplication and units.

Naturality of the normalized point cone, the constant-pullback comparison and the residue-tower isomorphism gives compatibility of reductions. Since multiplication by l^(n+2) factors as multiplication by l followed by multiplication by l^(n+1), the latter quotient projection kills it. Its cokernel universal property constructs the transition. Cancel the epic quotient projection and use the comparison projection equations to prove the transition square. Choose the levelwise structures and isomorphisms to assemble all positive exponents.

Also read the cited statements: sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x (E=Q_l, a ring isomorphism R_X ≅ lim A_n for any scheme), sectionwise-limits 00W2, constant sheaf 0H7J, sections-local 00WK, algebra-hom-quotient, locally-bijective criterion and sheafification 00WH. Coefficient check: R_X = p_X^* C(-,Z_l), the same object as O_{E,X} in sk-prop. rho_r is defined precisely as that isomorphism followed by the r-th projection. There is no base change, the statement is unchanged and not weakened, and the scope is arbitrary X with no l-invertibility needed. Steps: the cancellation l^{n+r} | l^r k <=> l^n | k gives the finite-label injection and its kernel. Labels pass to sections by local representatives and local equality. The identity red∘j_{n+1,r} = j_{n,r}∘red gives the compatible divided tuple, so ker rho_r(U) = l^r R_X(U) on every U. Integer lifts give local surjectivity. The presheaf quotient is sectionwise injective and locally surjective, so its sheafification is A_r; ring and module structures and the transition compatibility are checked on local representatives. All steps are correct and the elementary flags are fair. Small cases: empty X, r=1, characteristic l, a w-contractible U (C(S,Z_l)/l^r = C(S,Z/l^r)). Routes: sk-prop is on the unit's route, the three generic site-lemma tool_uses are accepted, the graph is acyclic, and there are no new nodes. lean.statement: theorem pur_condensed_zl_reduction_mod_ell_power (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (X : Scheme.{u}) : ∃ (m : ∀ n : ℕ, MonObj (purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 1)).X) (e : ∀ n : ℕ, purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 1) ≅ purZlResidueModule ℓ X (n + 1)), (∀ n : ℕ, @IsMonHom _ _ _ _ _ (coefficientRing X (Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj ℤ_[ℓ]))).mon (m n) (purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 1)).hom ∧ @IsMonHom _ _ _ _ _ (m n) ((sfbConstantRing X).obj ((sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ).obj (op (n + 1)))).mon (e n).hom.hom ∧ @IsMonHom _ _ _ _ _ ((sfbConstantRing X).obj ((sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ).obj (op (n + 1)))).mon (m n) (e n).inv.hom ∧ (purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 1)).hom ≫ (e n).hom.hom = (purZlReduction ℓ X (n + 1)).hom) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, purZlReduction ℓ X (n + 2) ≫ (sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ ⋙ sfbConstantRing X).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))).op = purZlReduction ℓ X (n + 1)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ t : purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 2) ⟶ purZlQuotient ℓ X (n + 1), purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 2) ≫ t = purZlQuotientProjection ℓ X (n + 1) ∧ t.hom ≫ (e n).hom.hom = (e (n + 1)).hom.hom ≫ ((sfbZModCoefficientTower ℓ ⋙ sfbConstantRing X).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))).op).hom)
lean.note: The canonical reduction is the normalized completed-coefficient limit projection, transported through its cyclic constant-ring comparisons. The sheaf quotient is Mod.cokernelObj of scalar multiplication. The single theorem supplies its quotient ring operations and a module isomorphism preserving ring operations in both directions, with the quotient projection equation and all positive-exponent transition squares. Helper definitions expose precisely these constructions; no dependency or natural-language statement is changed.
